newsitem.title: USA: NE Utils restores most storm power outages.
newsitem.headline: NE Utils restores most storm power outages.

text.p: Northeast Utilities has restored power to nearly all of its customers who were left without service after a weekend storm, a company spokesman said Thursday.
"There are some sporadic areas that will go down to do maintenance work today, but almost all customers now have service," the spokesman said.
Heavy, wet snow from the storm knocked trees onto power lines, leaving about 200,000 customers in Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Connecticut and Maine without power as of Sunday.

Although most power had been restored to Northeast Utilities customers as of Thursday morning, the spokesman said another approaching storm was nervously being watched and could bring further power line damage.
"The next storm is expected to hit late Friday or Saturday, and we don't know whether it will bring rain or ice or snow," the Northeast Utilities spokesman said.

Separately, COM/Electric, a subsidiary of Commonwealth Energy System said power was restored in most of Connecticut, western Massachusetts and southern New Hampshire Thursday morning following the weekend storm.
COM/Electric said it had sent over 70 linemen and maintenance personal to help restore power in the area.
COM/Electric said it serves 350,000 customers in southeastern Massachusetts, Cape Cod, Martha's Vineyard and Cambridge.
